$ cd /data/workspace/.claude/agent-memory/risk-assessor; cat >> builder_pitfalls.md <<'EOF'

7. **history.json schema drift crashes the builder before any risk is checked (2026-10-17).** `Method.__init__` expects `scoring_method.likelihood_scale` and `impact_scale` as *lists* of `{score, label, …}`, `combination.cells` as a list of 25 `{likelihood, impact, label, score_printed}`, and `corporate_register_threshold` keyed by reading (`table_4`, `figure_4`, each with `section` and `score_at_or_above`). A findings-analyst output with `{entries: […]}` scales, `matrix_rows` instead of `cells`, or a single flat CRR object gives a TypeError traceback (exit 1, nothing written).
   **Why:** the inputs and builder are read-only for this agent, so the run must stop. **How to apply:** if the builder dies in `Method`, compare these four keys first, then stop and report the mismatch so findings-analyst can be re-run. Do not reshape history.json yourself. Draft risk-ratings.json first anyway; it can be rebuilt once history.json is fixed.
EOF
sed -i 's/^- \[Builder pitfalls\](builder_pitfalls.md) — .*/- [Builder pitfalls](builder_pitfalls.md) — no [n] in citation tags; risk IDs and day counts trip the typed-figure check; where no-uplift reasons go; revision overrides; £ quotes use |int; post-build edits force rev+1; history.json scoring_method shape the builder needs/' MEMORY.md; cat MEMORY.md

I couldn't build the register: the builder crashes on `outputs/history.json`, so `outputs/risk-register.md` and `outputs/auditor-comments.md` were not written. There is nothing for the auditor to review yet.

This was a first run, since there was no comments file.

**Why it stopped:** the builder exited with code 1 and a crash (`TypeError` at `build_register.py:181`) before it checked any risk. The scoring method in `history.json` has all the right content, but it is laid out differently from what the builder expects:

| `scoring_method` key | Builder expects | `history.json` has |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `likelihood_scale`, `impact_scale` | a list of `{score, label, …}` | an object with the list under `entries` |
| `combination.cells` | 25 cells `{likelihood, impact, label, score_printed}` | no `cells`; `matrix_rows` instead |
| `corporate_register_threshold` | one entry per reading (`table_4`, `figure_4`), each with `section` and `score_at_or_above` | a single entry for Figure 4 only |

The third mismatch matters even once the crash is fixed. Without a Table 4 entry, the builder cannot use the Table 4 bands or mark the Figure 4 reading as the skill requires, and I'm not allowed to settle that discrepancy myself. I'm also not allowed to edit the inputs or the builder.

**To fix:** re-run findings-analyst so `history.json` uses the shape in the table above, then re-run me.

**What is ready:** `outputs/risk-ratings.json` is drafted and needs no changes for the rebuild. It has nine risks:
- **Rated from the spend data:** splitting below the threshold; payments clustered just below it; high-value suppliers with no matching contract notice; spend after every matched notice ended; spend above the award's annual rate; same-amount payments within a week.
- **Rated on the rule alone:** waivers, contract-award approvals and placement reasons can't be seen in public data, so these are scored "Unlikely" and the justifications say so.

All figures are placeholders and no supplier is named. None of these scores has been checked by the builder yet, so they are not ratings until it runs. Six themes are left out, each with a one-line reason; for example, the statutory-threshold tests can't run until the auditor supplies those figures.

Some rule numbers in the skill's theme table don't match the current `rules.json`. I used the numbers in `rules.json` (e.g. extensions under CPR-62, variations under CPR-63/64, placements under CPR-65).

**Memory:** I added one lesson to `builder_pitfalls.md`: the four `history.json` keys the builder needs, and to stop and report rather than reshape the file. No figures or ratings were saved.

Once the builder has run, the auditor's next step will be to record a decision (approve, amend or reject) for each risk in `outputs/auditor-comments.md`.
